title: WAT Hour-Manifest v2 — Multi-Capability Trigger + Optional Signature Slot
description: JSON-Schema for the WAT hour-manifest v2 envelope (multi-capability trigger). v2 is emitted iff at least one ingested frame in the hour has more than one capability-token reference (caprefs[]); hours where every frame has zero or one capref continue to emit v1 manifests. Schema is additive over v1: every v1 field MUST validate identically here, and v2 adds two top-level keys (multi_cap_events, multi_cap_summary). 0.2.0 (Phase-2 Sprint-5 Tag-1) adds an additive optional top-level `signature` slot (Ed25519 detached-signature block) that is valid on BOTH wat-manifest/1.0 and wat-manifest/2.0 envelopes; absence is permitted (legacy unsigned manifests continue to validate). Slot shape mirrors wirelang.identity.aip_signing / wirelang.schemas.entry_signing / wat.identity.manifest_signing byte-for-byte. See docs/wat-manifest-v2-multi-cap-stub.md and docs/wat-manifest-v2-spec.md §4.4 / §11 (Sprint-5 Tag-1) for the full spec, trigger condition, verifier behaviour, signing semantics, and open questions. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

version.description: Manifest version discriminator. v1 hours retain wat-manifest/1.0 verbatim. v2 hours (at least one frame with len(caprefs) > 1) emit wat-manifest/2.0 and MUST populate multi_cap_events + multi_cap_summary. Verifier and audit-query both fall back to v1 semantics on v1 manifests.

hour_slot.description: UTC hour slot in YYYY-MM-DDTHH form. Same shape as v1 manifests and TV-1/TV-2/TV-3 driver harnesses.

merkle_root.description: SHA-256 hex of the canonical Merkle root over the events[] leaves[] for this hour. Identical derivation as v1; multi-cap metadata does NOT affect the merkle_root computation. The merkle_root is what gets OTS-stamped against the public Bitcoin calendar substrate.

event_count.description: Number of audit-event frames ingested for this hour. Equal to len(events) and len(leaves).

events.description: Per-event metadata array, schema unchanged from v1. Each item carries event_id, leaf hash, and the v1-projected capability_token_hash (= caprefs[0] when caprefs is non-empty). Multi-cap frames are still represented here with caprefs[0] for backwards-compatible v1 audit queries; the full caprefs[] set is exposed separately under multi_cap_events.

leaves.description: Ordered SHA-256 leaf hashes feeding the Merkle tree, one per event.

tree_levels.description: Reconstructable Merkle tree levels (leaves at index 0, root at last index). Used for inclusion-proof rebuilding by the verifier without re-walking the leaves.

build_time.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which the manifest was constructed by the aggregator. Informational only; not part of the merkle_root computation.

multi_cap_events.description: Per-event multi-capability sidecar. Present iff version == wat-manifest/2.0. Keys are event_id strings (matching events[].event_id). Each value carries the verbatim caprefs[] list as the producer emitted it plus a deterministic caprefs_root hash. Events with len(caprefs) <= 1 are NOT included here even on v2 manifests — only events that actually trigger the v2 condition.

caprefs_full.description: Verbatim ordered list of capability-token-hash references as the producer emitted them in caprefs[]. Order is significant — see open question 1 in the stub spec; current proposal is ordered Merkle (preserves producer intent), pending wirelang-engineering Zone-2 sign-off. minItems: 2 because by the trigger condition only events with >1 capref appear here.

caprefs_root.description: SHA-256 hex of the canonical Merkle root over caprefs_full. Pinned hash so audit queries do not need to iterate the full list to compare two events; verifier re-derives this root and rejects on mismatch. Ordered semantics (proposal): the Merkle preserves caprefs_full ordering verbatim. Sorted semantics (alternative): caprefs_full is sorted lexicographically before Merkle. Open question 1 in the stub spec.

multi_cap_summary.description: Hour-level multi-capability roll-up. Present iff version == wat-manifest/2.0. Pure summary; brand-page and ops-dashboard render this without scanning the per-event sidecar. All counts are integers; producers MUST keep them consistent with multi_cap_events.

events_with_multi_cap.description: Count of events in this hour with len(caprefs) > 1. By the trigger condition this is >= 1 on v2 manifests.

max_caprefs_in_any_event.description: Largest len(caprefs) observed in any event in this hour. By the trigger condition this is >= 2 on v2 manifests.

distinct_capability_token_hashes_in_hour.description: Count of distinct capability_token_hash values across the union of caprefs[] from all events in this hour (v2 frames + v1-equivalent caprefs[0] from single-cap frames). Useful for audit-query 'how many capabilities were exercised in hour H?'.

signature.description: Optional detached Ed25519 signature block over the canonical (JCS-canonicalised, SHA-256-hashed) manifest payload with the `signature` slot removed. Additive on both wat-manifest/1.0 and wat-manifest/2.0 envelopes (Phase-2 Sprint-5 Tag-1, schema 0.2.0). Absence is permitted: legacy unsigned manifests continue to validate. Slot shape is byte-identical to wirelang.identity.aip_signing.SIGNATURE_BLOCK, wirelang.schemas.entry_signing._validate_signature_block_shape, and wat.identity.manifest_signing.SIGNATURE_FIELD. The kid field references an AIP-document public_keys entry under PURPOSE_WAT_ANCHOR; the resolver bridge is wat.identity.anchor_kid.resolve_wat_anchor_kid (Sprint-4 Tag-5). The signing primitive (wat.identity.manifest_signing.sign_manifest, Sprint-4 Tag-6) emits exactly this shape.

alg.description: Signature algorithm identifier. Closed enum: only Ed25519 is accepted today; future algorithm support requires a coordinated additive schema bump and a parallel allowlist entry in wat.identity.manifest_signing.SIGNATURE_ALG.

kid.description: Key identifier. Non-empty string. Caller binds this to an AIP-document public_keys entry under PURPOSE_WAT_ANCHOR (see wat.identity.anchor_kid).

signature.description: Ed25519 detached signature, 64 bytes encoded as 128 lowercase hex chars. Pre-image: SHA-256 of the RFC-8785 JCS canonicalisation of the manifest payload with this `signature` slot stripped.

then.description: v2 manifests MUST carry both multi_cap_events and multi_cap_summary. Trigger condition guarantees multi_cap_events has at least one entry.
v1 manifests MUST NOT carry multi-cap sidecar keys. Producers that find themselves about to emit multi_cap_* on a v1 manifest have a trigger-condition bug.
